lead_note: Aaron 11:15 PT: rerun on the same packet; medium verdict was GO. HIGH finds 3 blockers; blocker 3 (open-short warning fires on Questrade/sell-side) overlaps the Opus MAJOR finding; the compound-code miss ('A;O') that Opus called the main defect is only advisory 3 here. Not reproduced by the lead; the hidden reference tests (35/37, two behavioural failures) already confirm the assignment and opening-short defects.

blockers.claim: The assignment/exercise pairing takes the first unused same-day share row for the same underlying without checking side or quantity. Reproduce: buy 100 AAPL on 1/2, short put open on 1/5, then on 3/1 list an ordinary sell of 100 AAPL before the option row (code A, +1) and the share buy (100, code A). The premium is attached to the ordinary sell's event instead of the assignment buy.

A premium stamped on a share row that sells while close == 0 (no held shares) is popped at line 213 and never consumed: the sell branch only uses roll_delta inside 'if close > 0', and the remainder path ignores it. The option pool cost is already reduced, so the credit vanishes with no premium warning. Reproduce: short call open (sell -1 @3.0, code O) on 1/5; on 3/1 option buy +1 @3.0 code A, then sell -100 @160 code A with no earlier AAPL buy in the file. Only the generic nothing-held warning fires.

The new nothing-held warning now fires for option sells that have no code or a non-O action, so a Questrade opening short option (action SELL, no O/C codes, no prior position) gets 'sold ... with nothing held'. The brief asked for this warning only on closing trades, and Questrade rows cannot tell open from close. Reproduce: Questrade CSV with one option SELL -1 and nothing before it; a warning is produced where none was before.

advisories.claim: Line 213 pops _roll_cad from the caller's Transaction.raw, so the input object is mutated; a stamp left by an early exit or a re-run with a different as_of carries over.
_last_event_for matches events by fingerprint; if two rows share a fingerprint, the premium lands on the wrong event. Confirm fingerprints are unique per row.
ASSIGN_EXERCISE_CODES and _roll_code use exact matches; if the IBKR Code cell can hold several codes at once, a combined cell such as 'Ex;C' is treated as an ordinary trade.
Only the activity-statement Comm/Fee line is changed. grep for other abs() calls on Comm/Fee, such as the ibkr_flex path, to confirm rebates are handled the same way.
Line 537 reads the key 'other_income'. The diff does not show the Settings page's key, and test_ui_smoke writes that key directly, so the test does not prove the box mirrors the Settings field.

Lines 508-515 credit all of other_income against the business CPP, but the field comment at line 494 says it includes pensions, which are not payroll-pensionable. For job income this is right; the comment should say so, or pension recipients get an understated self-employed CPP.

tests: Covers long-call exercise, short-put assignment in both file orders, long-put exercise, Questrade ASN, the orphan and open-short warnings, the rebate sign, the CPP band split and the summary card; misses a sell-side assignment (short call), a same-day ordinary trade beside an assignment, Questrade EXE, and the ibkr_flex parser.
brief_mistakes: The brief does not say how to pair an assignment with its share row when several same-day rows exist, does not cover short-call assignment or short-stock delivery, and does not note that Questrade rows cannot tell an opening option sell from a closing one.
